title: Measures to Optimise Outpatient Appointments and Unified Appointment Tracking System for Polyclinics and Restructured Hospitals
what_it_is: Measures to Optimise Outpatient Appointments and Unified Appointment Tracking System for Polyclinics and Restructured Hospitals

sections.label: Outpatient appointment scheduling and consolidation
sections.summary: MOH lacks age-stratified appointment data but hospitals schedule and consolidate outpatient appointments, with pilots and plans to harmonise across clusters.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether the Ministry studies the median and 90th percentile number of outpatient appointments per patient, stratified by age; (b) what measures are in place to optimise the number of outpatient appointments as part of holistic healthcare; and (c) whether elderly patients with multiple outpatient appointments can have them converged on the same days where possible to reduce caregiver stress and repeat blood tests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Ministry of Health (MOH) does not have data on the median and 90th percentile number of outpatient appointments per patient stratified by age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our public healthcare institutions have put in place systems to allow patients to schedule their outpatient appointments together where possible because we understand this will be more convenient for patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Our hospitals have also started to consolidate Specialist Outpatient Clinic appointments from different specialties so that patients need to make fewer visits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: At the Singapore General Hospital, diabetic patients visiting the Diabetes and Metabolic Centre can make appointments for related specialties and services, such as podiatry, eye, orthopaedic surgery, on the same day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As I have mentioned earlier, this is with the intent of bringing about greater convenience and better care for our patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will be piloting more of such systems across institutions within our healthcare clusters to facilitate better appointment, rationalisation and reconciliation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: MOH will also study the next step of harmonising appointments across our three healthcare clusters.

sections.label: Coordinated care across clusters
sections.summary: The whole care spectrum is coordinated through Regional Health Systems and three clusters, which will reach out to private and community partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Primary care, the acute care in hospital, the step-down care, community hospitals, home care, community care, long-term care, so, that whole spectrum is coordinated through our Regional Health Systems and now we have three clusters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is why I mentioned earlier that we will work through our clusters to reach out to not just the public healthcare institutions, but also our partners in the private sector and in the community.
